Finish the donation or handover arrangements before the moving day. A bag marked “charity” still needs somewhere confirmed to go. Do not include unwanted possessions in the van on the assumption the driver will dispose of them.

Give kitchen items enough packing time

Wash and dry anything you intend to keep. Wrap plates, glasses and mugs individually, using a sturdy box and enough padding to prevent movement. Put heavier pieces at the bottom without creating a box that is difficult to lift.

Seal dry ingredients securely if you are taking them. Avoid putting food beside documents, clothing or electronics. Plan meals before leaving so you are not left trying to transport a freezer full of food. Check any storage provider’s rules before packing consumables for a longer stay.

Keep one small cleaning kit available until the room and your agreed shared areas have been dealt with. Remember to include that kit in your final check. It is easy to pack the mop early and find that the area beneath your boxes still needs attention.

Choose one destination or clearly label several

If you are moving straight into a shared house, confirm key collection and which room is yours. Ask whether anyone else will be unloading at the same time. That conversation can prevent two collections arriving together with nobody available to organise the space.

If part of the load is going home, mark those boxes separately. Our university moving-home guide helps with planning that journey. For belongings waiting for the next address, arrange your unit and then book student storage transport. Frank’s moves the load; you arrange the storage space.

A different destination means more information for the quote. List every stop and what must be delivered there. Do not add a drop-off informally on the day, because it can change the route, loading order and time required.

Ask the right access questions

The university’s reception information groups Sheavyn House with Ashburne Hall. That identifies the administrative contact point; it does not establish the loading point for your departure.

Ask for current collection instructions, then send the mover your exact block, flat, room and floor. Confirm where the van may stop, whether its registration is required and how you should meet the driver. Explain any stairs, awkward turns or longer carrying distances that you have established.

Check the same details at the destination. For a broader checklist covering both ends, see our University of Manchester removals guide.

Finish with a full-room and shared-space check

Work through the room in a set order: wardrobe, drawers, shelves, under the bed, behind the door and any bathroom storage. Then check the places outside your room where you have kept belongings. Include laundry, bicycles and items lent to friends in your list.

Take appropriate dated photographs after clearing the space and follow your departure instructions for returning keys. Keep your identification, phone and essential medication with you. A finished move means your own possessions are accounted for and the remaining shared items have an agreed owner, rather than an unanswered message in the flat chat.

title: Moving Out of Hulme Hall and Burkhardt House
seoTitle: Hulme Hall & Burkhardt House Moving Guide | Frank’s
description: Plan a move from Hulme Hall or Burkhardt House in Victoria Park, with clear address details, packing steps, shared bookings and storage options.
excerpt: Neighbouring residences need clear collection details. Use the correct hall, room and Victoria Park address when arranging your move.
bodyHtml:
The most useful first step when moving from Hulme Hall or Burkhardt House is simple: give everyone helping you the full, correct address. A familiar hall name may be enough for a friend on campus, but a driver needs the residence, room details and confirmed approach.

These are neighbouring University of Manchester residences in Victoria Park. The university’s Burkhardt House profile identifies its location beside Hulme Hall and its use of Hulme reception. A shared reception does not mean that every resident has the same room, entrance or carrying route.

Avoid the Hulme address mix-up

Use “Hulme Hall, Victoria Park” when describing the collection, and include the full address from your accommodation paperwork. Do not rely on “Hulme” by itself. If you live in Burkhardt House, put that name prominently in the booking as well.

Add the block, flat or room, floor and a contact number. Send any residence-approved loading instructions separately from a general map pin. The mover should be able to identify the collection without relying on a remembered route to another Manchester address.

Our University of Manchester removals guide explains the information needed for a student booking. It is worth checking the destination address with the same care, especially if your next house has more than one entrance.

Start with the room you actually occupy

The official Hulme Hall profile describes catered accommodation, while Burkhardt is self-catered. Your own belongings, shared purchases and next address will determine what needs to move.

Walk through your room and list everything that belongs to you. Then check the shared areas. If you have mostly used catering, do not assume you need to buy a whole kitchen before leaving: ask what the next property and your future housemates already provide.

At Burkhardt, pay particular attention to the kitchen cupboards and equipment bought together. Agree who is taking shared items and complete any handovers before the departure day. Leave accommodation furniture and equipment according to the inventory.

Prepare a useful booking note

Booking detailWhat to include
ResidenceHulme Hall or Burkhardt House, with the full Victoria Park address.
Room locationBlock, flat or room and floor.
BelongingsBoxes, cases, furniture you own and awkward items.
AccessConfirmed stopping point and carrying route.
TimingYour departure deadline and destination key availability.
Help requiredWho is carrying, and any assistance you need.

Use this note when asking for a student man and van quote. Photographs of larger items can clarify what you mean by “a few bits”. Include the bike, laundry rack and any exercise equipment rather than adding them once the vehicle arrives.

Consider a shared booking carefully

If a friend in the neighbouring hall is moving on the same day, a combined collection may be worth pricing. It still involves two room locations and potentially separate carrying routes. Provide both inventories and any extra destination before the quote is agreed.

Choose one lead contact and label every box with a person and destination. Agree the collection order with the mover, then make sure both loads are ready. A friend’s late packing should not leave you unable to complete your own departure on time.

Sharing is a planning option, not a guaranteed saving. Compare the quoted arrangements and make sure the timing works for each person. If the deadlines or destinations clash, separate moves may be easier to organise.

Check the gap between rooms

Look at when you must leave and when you can actually enter the next property. If there is a gap, arrange a confirmed place for the belongings. Do not assume a friend can keep a roomful of boxes without checking their space and permission.

For a trip back to the family home, use our moving home guide to organise the load. If storage is the answer, book the unit yourself and ask Frank’s about transport to the storage space. Check its opening hours and access process before agreeing collection.

Keep checkout separate from loading

Allow a finishing period after the van is loaded. Check drawers, shelves, hooks and shared cupboards, then take the photographs needed for your own records. Keep enough cleaning supplies available to deal with the cleared room.

Follow the residence’s instructions for returning keys and recording your departure. Keep your keys, documents and phone in a bag you carry. Clear naming, a complete inventory and a confirmed destination give this move a straightforward shape, even when several people are helping.

faqs.answer: Confirm the departure loading point with the residence. Sharing a reception does not establish where a collection vehicle may stop or where boxes should wait.

faqs.answer: Usually they can be included in the same inventory, provided they are appropriately packed. Wrap fragile pieces, secure containers and keep liquids away from electronics and paperwork.

faqs.answer: Label each item or box with its destination and tell the mover about all stops when requesting the quote. Book any required storage separately before collection.

title: Moving Out of Dalton-Ellis Hall
seoTitle: Moving Out of Dalton-Ellis Hall | Student Moving Guide
description: Organise your Dalton-Ellis Hall move around study commitments, packing, block access and a clear collection plan for home, another room or storage.
excerpt: Break the move into manageable jobs so your last week is not spent choosing between revision and an unpacked room.
bodyHtml:
Moving out of Dalton-Ellis Hall does not need to consume your final week at university. The useful approach is to split the job into things you can decide early, things you can pack gradually and a small set of tasks that genuinely need to wait until the last day.

Start with the departure deadline and next address. Then make the transport plan fit around your actual commitments. Our end-of-term moving guide is useful if packing is competing with coursework, work shifts or travel arrangements.

Identify the block and the route out

The official Dalton-Ellis profile describes several blocks and room types. Tell your mover which block and floor you occupy, rather than assuming the hall name alone describes the job.

Walk the route from your door to the residence’s permitted collection point. Note stairs, doors and any awkward turns. Ask about access arrangements you cannot confirm yourself, including whether a lift may be used for belongings. An access feature in another block does not establish what is available for your room.

Give the same information for the destination. If you are going to a house, ask about its entrance and stairs. If a parent or friend is receiving the load, make sure they know the agreed delivery arrangements and can be contacted.

Deal with decisions before boxes

Deciding what to keep is often slower than packing it. Sort out borrowed books, shared purchases and anything you intend to sell or give away before you start sealing boxes. Arrange actual handovers rather than adding those jobs to your departure morning.

Check what the next room contains before moving furniture or buying replacements. Keep supplied furniture at the hall according to your inventory. For personal furniture you are taking, send photographs and measurements when requesting a quote.

The university publishes licence agreement dates, but your own agreement and departure instructions should be beside you while planning. Record the checkout time as well as the date, and leave space after loading for the room handover.

Use a packing plan that protects study time

WhenUseful job
As soon as the next address is knownCheck access dates and decide whether storage is needed.
Before the busiest study periodSort belongings and request an accurate transport quote.
In short packing sessionsBox unused clothes, spare bedding and books you no longer need.
After the last usePack course equipment and electronics with their cables.
The evening beforeFinish labels and keep essentials in a separate bag.
After collectionCheck, clean, photograph and complete the key handover.

Use realistic sessions rather than assuming you will pack an entire room after an exhausting day. A clearly labelled box finished early is one less decision later. Keep the resources needed for your next deadline accessible until they are no longer required.

Pack books and equipment with care

Books, notes and folders become heavy quickly. Use small, strong boxes and avoid mixing sharp or fragile objects into gaps. Label any coursework you may need during the break so it can be found without unpacking everything.

Back up your important files before disconnecting a computer. Photograph cable connections, pack accessories together and protect screens with appropriate materials. Keep essential devices and valuable documents with you where practical, rather than burying them in an unmarked box.

Include unusual items in the inventory: a bicycle, instrument case, large monitor or sports equipment all affect how the load is arranged. Tell the mover if you have handling requirements that need discussing before the booking is agreed.

Choose between a direct move and storage

If you can enter the next property before leaving Dalton-Ellis, a direct transfer may be the simplest arrangement. Confirm key collection and somebody’s availability to let the movers in. Our student man and van service can be quoted for that route.

If you are leaving Manchester, our moving home from university guide helps organise a longer journey. If your belongings need to wait for the next accommodation, arrange a storage unit first, then discuss student storage transport. Frank’s provides the moving service; the storage space is booked by you.

Make the last day a short checklist

Keep keys, medication, identification, chargers and travel documents in a personal bag. Leave basic cleaning materials available. Check cupboards, under the bed, bathroom storage and any shared area where you have belongings.

Take the final photographs and follow the residence’s departure instructions. If anything about access has changed, tell the mover promptly. With the larger decisions already made, the last day can focus on checking the load and handing over the room, rather than trying to organise the whole move at once.

faqs.question: What information does a mover need for Dalton-Ellis Hall?
faqs.answer: Provide your block, room and floor, the confirmed collection access, the inventory and the full destination details. Mention any awkward or fragile items separately.

faqs.question: Can I pack before my course finishes?
faqs.answer: Pack items you will not need first, while keeping study materials, essential clothing and daily equipment accessible. Use a separate bag for the things required immediately before and after the move.

faqs.answer: No. Confirm the route that applies to your own room and whether any available lift can be used for the move. Give the mover the confirmed details.

faqs.question: How should I pack lots of books?
faqs.answer: Use several small, sturdy boxes rather than one large, very heavy container. Tape them securely, protect against moisture and label the contents so you can find needed material later.

faqs.question: What if my belongings are ready before I want to travel home?
faqs.answer: Ask about a collection date that works with your agreement and the receiving address. Keep your travel essentials separate, and make sure someone authorised can accept the delivery.

title: Moving Out of Canterbury Court and St Anselm Hall

Use the full hall and block name

Plan the carrying before filling the boxes

Canterbury Court’s official profile states that the hall has no lifts. If you live there, tell the mover the floor and describe the staircase route. At St Anselm, confirm the actual route from your room rather than making assumptions from another residence.

Keep boxes manageable and closed securely. Large bags can be difficult to carry if they have weak handles or loose contents. Break dense loads into smaller containers, and pack awkward objects separately so their shape is clear when you describe the job.

CheckAction

Carrying routeRecord stairs and any confirmed access arrangements.
DatesUse your agreement and the destination’s confirmed access time.
LoadCount boxes and cases, then list larger items separately.
Final handoverKeep time for cleaning, checking and returning keys.

Check whether sharing the move really works

A shared collection can be worth discussing if you and a friend have compatible dates and destinations. Work out the combined load before asking for a price. Two lightly packed rooms can look very different from two rooms containing bicycles, monitors and personal furniture.

List each collection point and delivery address. Choose one contact for the booking, agree how costs are divided and label every item by owner and destination. Give everyone a packing deadline that leaves time to solve small problems.

Prepare for the next room’s setup

Check the new property’s inventory before buying things or moving furniture. Find out what bed, desk and storage are provided. Agree kitchen purchases with new housemates, especially if people are coming from different catered or self-catered arrangements.

If you are going home, separate the things you will need during the break from the things intended for next term. Our moving home guide can help organise that journey. If there is a confirmed gap between addresses, book a suitable unit and ask about transport into student storage.

Frank’s handles moving belongings to storage you arrange. Check the provider’s opening hours, access procedure and restrictions before confirming the collection date. Keep documents, medication and anything needed during the gap with you.

Leave the room ready for handover

Once your load is out, check drawers, shelves, hooks and any shared storage you have used. Confirm that jointly owned items have an agreed destination and that supplied furniture remains where required.

Complete the cleaning and photographs before returning keys according to your instructions. Keep a small personal bag for essential items and paperwork. Clear room details and a realistic carrying plan give both you and the mover something concrete to work from.

faqs.question: Do Canterbury Court and St Anselm residents have identical agreements?

At Denmark Road, checking the agreement you actually signed is more useful than copying a moving date from another resident. A building name does not tell a mover when your room must be empty or when your next place becomes available.

Once those times are clear, the practical plan is straightforward: identify your load, confirm access and arrange transport to a destination that is ready. Our University of Manchester student removals guide provides the broader moving checklist.

Check how you booked the room

Do not use an advertised agreement length to calculate a leaving date yourself. Read the actual end date and ask your accommodation contact to confirm anything unclear. Keep the checkout time and key-return process with that information.

Send the mover the date you have confirmed, not a screenshot of an unrelated room offer. This also matters if you are moving with a friend: each resident should check their own arrangement before a shared booking is made.

Build the handover around two addresses

Check when you can obtain the keys to the destination. If somebody else is receiving the load, confirm their availability and the place where belongings should be put. Include the destination floor and access route in the quote request.

A departure deadline and a new tenancy start date are not necessarily a workable moving window by themselves. Add the practical times: key collection, loading, travel, unloading and returning the old key. Leave enough room to finish the old room properly.

Give the mover room-level details

Include the flat, room and floor, and explain the route from your room to the permitted stopping point. Ask the residence about any arrangements needed for moving belongings, such as access doors or use of a lift. Pack the room, kitchen and en suite as separate jobs

Check kitchen cupboards for personal items, then agree what happens to shared purchases. Wash and dry what you are keeping. Wrap breakables and separate any liquids from dry belongings. Remove food according to the residence’s instructions rather than assuming a flatmate will take it.

For the bathroom, set aside the toiletries you need on the final morning. Pack the rest securely, checking lids and keeping anything that could leak in a suitable separate container. Keep cleaning supplies out until the empty spaces have been dealt with.

Plan any storage before booking the transport

If you are returning to the family home, check how much space is available there and read our moving home from university guide. Split home and storage belongings before collection, with clear destination labels and a list of what goes where.

Keep the final checkout organised

After loading, inspect the cleared room and the areas where you kept belongings. Take appropriate dated photographs and follow the departure instructions for keys and any required records. Keep your identification, valuables and phone with you throughout.

The best moving plan at Denmark Road comes from your own confirmed agreement. Once that is paired with accurate access details and a ready destination, the rest can be organised around a clear, practical collection.

faqs.question: Do all Denmark Road residents have the same leaving date?

Plan the delivery before the room is emptied

Separate checkout from the vehicle timetable

Stay contactable while the collection is approaching. If building access or the agreed stopping point changes, let the mover know promptly. Good information about the actual route gives your Weston Hall move a better start than relying on a nearby landmark or an old parking tip.

faqs.question: Can I tell the van to use Charles Street Car Park?

excerpt: A practical departure plan for Piccadilly Point residents, from confirming checkout to sending belongings home or into storage.
bodyHtml:
Moving out of Piccadilly Point is easier to organise when you separate two journeys: where your belongings are going and how you are travelling yourself. They may have the same destination, but they do not have to leave together.

Unite Students lists Piccadilly Point at 23 Berry Street, Manchester, M1 2AD. Use the full property name and address when requesting a collection. “Near Piccadilly” is not precise enough for a booking, especially when the mover also needs your flat, floor and building instructions.

Confirm the final day of your booking

Check the end date in your own accommodation account or agreement. Your last exam, a housemate’s departure and the end of teaching are not substitutes for the date you have booked the room until.

Unite’s current checkout guidance says your room and kitchen must be clean and empty before 10am on the final tenancy day. Check the property’s messages for your arrangements and ask the team promptly if you foresee a problem. Do not treat an afternoon van booking as permission to stay beyond checkout.

Work backwards from that deadline. Allow for carrying the belongings out, checking storage spaces, clearing your part of the kitchen and returning keys as instructed. If your travel plans make the final morning difficult, consider arranging transport for an earlier day you are permitted to use.

Make a Berry Street collection brief

Ask the property team how collections should work. A nearby road, station or car park does not automatically provide a permitted loading point. The useful answer is the current instruction for your building, including any arrangements for a van and the route from your room.

Tell the moverWhy it helps
Piccadilly Point, 23 Berry Street, M1 2ADIdentifies the correct residence
Flat, floor and roomDescribes where the load starts
Confirmed building instructionsAllows collection to be planned within the rules
Box count and photographsMakes the size of the load clearer
Delivery address and access timePrevents a journey to a destination that is not ready

Ask about lift use if you will need it, but do not assume exclusive access or a reserved slot. Leave shared routes clear, and agree where you should meet the mover rather than carrying boxes into a communal entrance without permission.

Pack the room you have actually occupied

Piccadilly Point offers both ensuite rooms with shared kitchens and studios. Your packing list should reflect your own accommodation. In a shared flat, identify your food, pans and utensils before somebody else packs them. In a studio, check every cupboard rather than concentrating on the visible belongings around the bed.

Keep supplied furniture and appliances on the accommodation inventory. Only include items you own in the moving load. If you bought a chair, shelving unit or other larger item during the year, send its dimensions and a photograph with the quote request.

Number the containers and keep a simple note of what is in each. Make a separate “travel with me” bag for documents, keys, medicines, chargers and anything needed during the next day. Once the main load has left, that bag should still be within reach.

Choose home, another room or storage

For a move to another Manchester address, confirm the new room is accessible before agreeing delivery. Our student moving service can be quoted using both addresses, your inventory and the access details. Tell us if the delivery includes stairs or several people’s belongings.

If you are going home, decide whether everything needs to travel with you. Compare the complete arrangements, including carrying luggage on your own journey and receiving the remaining belongings at home. Our moving-home information for students provides a starting point for a separate transport enquiry.

If the next Manchester room is not ready, you can book a storage provider and request transport into storage. Frank’s handles the moving leg, not the storage contract. Confirm the unit or box service accepts your inventory and that the arrival time fits its access arrangements.

Keep your personal departure realistic

Being close to a station can make travelling onward convenient, but it does not remove the work of checking out. Avoid booking your own departure so tightly that a final room check becomes impossible. Keep some room in the timetable for the process you have agreed with reception.

Do not assume a removals booking includes a passenger place. Make your travel arrangements separately and ask how you will coordinate collection and delivery. If another person will meet the mover at the destination, give their details and make sure they know what is arriving.

Finish with a room-to-destination check

Before handing back access, check under the bed, inside drawers, bathroom storage, the kitchen and any bike or parcel arrangements you used. Photograph the empty room for your records and complete the property’s checkout process.

At delivery, use your numbered inventory to check the load. Put the first-night items somewhere easy to reach and save the storage paperwork if some belongings are staying in Manchester. Your move is complete when everything has an agreed destination, not simply when the bedroom looks empty.

faqs.answer: Use Piccadilly Point, 23 Berry Street, Manchester, M1 2AD, plus your flat, floor and room details. Ask the property team for the current collection instructions; the postal address does not establish where a van may stop.

faqs.question: What time do I need to leave Piccadilly Point?
faqs.answer: Unite’s published general guidance says the room and kitchen must be clean and empty before 10am on the final tenancy day. Check your agreement and the property’s instructions, and speak to the team if you need to discuss your departure.

faqs.question: Can my belongings go to storage while I travel home?
faqs.answer: Yes, subject to a confirmed transport booking and a suitable storage arrangement. You choose and book the storage provider. Give Frank’s the inventory, storage address, access requirements and contact for delivery; organise your own travel separately.

faqs.question: Can I put packed boxes in reception before collection?
faqs.answer: Ask the property team first. Do not assume reception provides storage or that shared entrances can be used for a waiting load. Follow the building’s current instructions.

faqs.question: Do I need to move the bed or desk?
faqs.answer: Only include furniture you own or have explicit permission to remove. Check the room inventory and leave supplied items in place as required by the accommodation provider.

title: Moving Out of Parkway Gate, Manchester
seoTitle: Moving Out of Parkway Gate, Manchester | Frank’s
description: A Parkway Gate moving-out plan covering your final room check, Chester Street collection, shared kitchen belongings and transport to home or storage.
excerpt: Organise your Parkway Gate departure in stages, with a practical final-day checklist and the details to include in a moving quote.
bodyHtml:
A useful Parkway Gate move-out plan leaves very little packing for the final morning. By then, your belongings should be counted, your delivery address confirmed and the property’s departure instructions understood. The last tasks should be the things you could not reasonably finish earlier.

The official Parkway Gate page gives the address as 50 Chester Street, Manchester, M15 6JH. Include your flat and room details when organising a collection, and identify the residence by name rather than giving “Chester Street” alone.

Write your own final-day timetable

Find your contract end date and check messages from the property team. Under Unite’s general checkout guidance, the departure deadline is before 10am on the final tenancy day. Confirm how the current instructions apply to your booking.

Use a timetable based on your actual collection, not an optimistic estimate of how quickly you can pack. If the load must leave early, finish the kitchen sorting and most cleaning the previous day. Keep a small bag for the items used overnight.

StageFinish these tasks
Several days beforeConfirm destination, request building instructions and count large items
Before the last eveningPack books, spare clothes, decorations and kitchen items you will not use
Last eveningCheck the inventory, seal boxes and prepare your travel bag
Before collectionPack remaining bedding and toiletries; keep keys available
After loadingComplete the final room check and the instructed key return

Sort the kitchen while everyone is still available

For an ensuite room with a shared kitchen, a flat conversation can prevent the most avoidable packing problems. Work through cupboard shelves, the fridge and freezer, and any items several people have used. Decide who owns what before putting it in a box.

If you live in a studio, check your own cupboards systematically. Start at one end, empty and clean a section, then move along. Do not place cleaned items back into a cupboard just because the room still has a few days left to run; put the things you have finished using into their moving containers.

Keep accommodation-owned appliances and furniture separate from your possessions. Use the original inventory where available, and ask the property team about anything uncertain. A kettle you bought and an appliance supplied with the room are different entries on a moving list.

Turn a roomful of belongings into a quote

Write down the number of boxes, suitcases and bags after a first packing pass. Add loose items individually, with dimensions for anything bulky. Photos are useful for objects that are difficult to describe, such as a large monitor setup or a shelving unit you assembled yourself.

Our Manchester student moving service can be quoted from this information. Include the destination, the floor at both ends and whether you need help carrying. Do not leave a bike, clothes airer or extra chair out because it is “only one more thing”.

For several residents moving together, identify each person’s load and all proposed stops. Ask whether the combined job is workable before agreeing a cost split. Friends leaving Parkway Gate on the same date may still have different delivery times or addresses.

Ask about the collection route

Check where the property team wants collections to take place and whether there are relevant arrangements for lifts, entrances or visitors. Pass those instructions to the mover. A statement about ordinary resident parking does not by itself establish the rules for a removal collection.

Keep packed belongings in the location the building permits until they are being moved. Stacking boxes in a corridor may appear to save time but can obstruct other residents and building access. Have your phone charged and agree where you will meet the collection team.

Plan the destination as carefully as the departure

For another Manchester room, confirm the address and when someone can receive the load. If you study at Manchester Met, our Manchester Metropolitan student removals page provides a broader starting point for the move. The incoming building’s instructions still need to be checked directly.

For a summer gap, choose a storage provider before arranging the journey. Check the space, accepted items, payment and access. Frank’s student storage moving service transports belongings to and from storage you book; it does not include a storage unit.

If the load is going home, tell the recipient what is arriving and when the delivery is expected. Make sure the agreed route into the house is clear. A bedroom’s contents do not become easier to receive simply because the destination is a family home.

Do one final sweep

Once the main load has gone, check drawers, underbed space, bathroom shelves, kitchen storage and any bike or parcel arrangements. Take a record of the empty room for yourself and follow the property’s checkout instructions.

Keep your departure documents and the moving quote on your phone. If plans change, contact the property team about accommodation and the mover about transport; they manage different parts of the day. For a quote from Frank’s, send the finished inventory and the confirmed collection and delivery details through the quote form.

faqs.question: What is Parkway Gate’s address for removals?
faqs.answer: Give Parkway Gate, 50 Chester Street, Manchester, M15 6JH, together with your flat, floor and room. Confirm the permitted collection arrangements with the property team before the move.

faqs.question: Can I leave packing until collection day?
faqs.answer: It is better to finish almost everything beforehand. Keep only overnight essentials unpacked, and leave time after loading for the room check and key return. The collection itself should not depend on finishing several boxes.

faqs.question: Can friends at Parkway Gate share a van?
faqs.answer: Ask for a group quote with separate inventories and every delivery address. A common residence helps identify the pickup, but the mover still needs to assess the total load, timings and destination access.

faqs.question: Should I take the room’s furniture?
faqs.answer: Only move belongings you own or have explicit permission to remove. Compare the room with its inventory and ask the property team about uncertain items before including them in the load.

faqs.question: Does Frank’s provide the summer storage?
faqs.answer: Frank’s provides transport to and from storage arranged by the customer. Book a suitable unit or service yourself, then share its location and access requirements when requesting the moving quote.

title: Moving Out of Artisan Heights
seoTitle: Moving Out of Artisan Heights, Manchester | Frank’s
description: Plan your Artisan Heights move with a room inventory, collection questions, fragile-item packing and transport to your next room, home or storage.
excerpt: Leaving Artisan Heights? Build a practical collection plan around your room, fragile belongings and the destination that will receive them.
secondaryKeywords: Artisan Heights Manchester man and van
bodyHtml:
At Artisan Heights, the useful moving question is not just how many boxes you have. It is how those boxes will get from your room to the agreed collection point, then into the room or storage space waiting at the other end.

Unite Students identifies Artisan Heights as 3 New Wakefield Street, Manchester, M1 5AA, beside Oxford Road station. Give the full residence address when enquiring about removals. Then add your own floor, flat and room, because the street address describes only the start of the carrying route.

Map the collection in questions

Ask the property team what residents need to arrange for a move-out collection. Write the answers down and send them with your booking enquiry. Do not assume that a lift, entrance or nearby stopping place can be used in a particular way without checking.

  • Where should the mover meet you, and who provides entry?
  • What is the permitted route from your room to the collection point?
  • Are there any arrangements you need to make for lift use?
  • Where should packed belongings remain until loading begins?
  • How should you complete checkout after your belongings leave?

These are questions to establish the current arrangements, not a description of reserved access at Artisan Heights. Share any restrictions before the quote is confirmed, including a collection deadline or a request to keep an entrance clear.

Make an inventory that includes your study setup

A student room can contain several small items that need more attention than their size suggests: a monitor, desktop computer, speakers, camera equipment or an instrument. List them separately rather than counting the desk area as one box.

Take photographs of your equipment before disconnecting it. Label cables for your own benefit and put small accessories into identifiable bags. If you have suitable original packaging, check it is complete and in good condition; if not, describe the item and discuss protection with the mover before the day.

Inventory entryUseful detail
Numbered boxesCount, approximate dimensions and any fragile contents
SuitcasesNumber and whether handles and wheels work
Monitor or computerDimensions, packaging and detachable parts
Personal furnitureSize, weight concerns and any dismantling required
Other loose itemsBike, airer, sports kit or instrument, listed separately

Leave supplied furniture and appliances with the accommodation. If something was present when you arrived, check the room inventory before treating it as yours. For shared flats, identify your kitchen possessions while flatmates are still available to answer questions.

Set the date from your agreement

Check your own booking end date rather than relying on university term dates. Unite’s general checkout deadline is before 10am on the final tenancy day; confirm the instructions for your departure with the property team.

Tell the mover the deadline and explain what remains to be done afterwards. You may need time to inspect the empty room, collect the last small items and return access devices. Packing should already be complete, apart from the essentials used overnight.

If you are booking an earlier collection, decide where you will stay and which belongings remain with you until departure. An earlier van does not change your accommodation agreement, but it may make your own travel day easier to organise.

Match the delivery to your next step

Moving to another Manchester address calls for a confirmed handover. Ask when you can enter the new room, how keys are collected and whether anybody else needs to be present. Our student man and van service can be quoted using this information and your completed inventory.

If your next accommodation starts later, book storage that accepts the load and gives you workable access. Frank’s can arrange transport to a customer-booked storage space. Keep anything needed during the gap with you, especially documents and study equipment you still use.

For belongings going beyond Manchester, use our moving-home page to plan the enquiry. Give the full delivery postcode and the recipient’s access details. Being close to Oxford Road station may help with your personal journey, but a removals booking should not be assumed to include passenger travel.

Pack for identification, not just containment

Number boxes on more than one side and keep a matching inventory on your phone. Add the destination room or “storage” where loads are being divided. Avoid loose bags of unrelated small objects; they are difficult to check at both ends and easy to confuse with rubbish during the final clean.

Keep an essentials bag separate and clearly mark it as staying with you. Include your room keys until the checkout procedure is finished. Check drawers and shelves after the main load leaves, when it is easier to see what remains.

Send one complete quote request

Combine the inventory, photographs, building instructions, destination and dates into one message. Say what carrying help you need and mention any item you cannot safely handle yourself. Ask what the quote includes rather than estimating from the journey distance alone.

You can send the details through Frank’s moving quote form. If the inventory or building arrangements change, update the booking before collection so the agreed job still matches the move.

faqs.question: Can the mover reserve or use a lift?
faqs.answer: Ask the accommodation team what arrangements apply. Do not assume a reservation or permission is included in a moving booking. Pass any instructions to the mover before agreeing the collection.

faqs.question: How should I include a monitor in the quote?
faqs.answer: List it separately, give the dimensions and explain what packaging you have. A photograph helps. Discuss protection and handling in advance instead of placing an unpackaged screen among ordinary boxes.

faqs.question: Can I send some items home and some to storage?
faqs.answer: Ask for both destinations to be quoted and label the loads clearly. Confirm access and a recipient at each stop. You must book any storage separately and check that it accepts your items.

faqs.question: Can I travel in the moving van?
faqs.answer: Do not assume passenger travel is included. Ask about the specific booking and organise your own transport unless an arrangement has been expressly confirmed. Make sure someone can receive the belongings at delivery.

title: Moving Out of New Medlock House
seoTitle: Moving Out of New Medlock House, Manchester | Frank’s
description: A New Medlock House move-out guide covering flatmates’ belongings, packing, Chester Street collection, checkout and your next Manchester address.
excerpt: Sort shared-flat belongings, confirm your New Medlock House departure and prepare a clear collection plan before the moving day.
secondaryKeywords: New Medlock House man and van
bodyHtml:
Leaving New Medlock House involves more than packing the things visible in your bedroom. Your belongings may also be in shared cupboards, the kitchen, bike storage or somebody else’s room. Start by gathering your own inventory while you still have time to speak to flatmates.

Unite Students lists New Medlock House at 25–45 Chester Street, Manchester, M15 6JX. Manchester Met’s official accommodation page identifies it as a private partner owned and managed by Unite. Use your accommodation agreement and the property team’s instructions for checkout, even if you applied through the university.

Start with ownership, then start packing

Walk through the flat with a note on your phone. Mark items as yours, a flatmate’s, shared or supplied by the accommodation. Anything uncertain stays out of the moving boxes until you have resolved it.

This is particularly useful for kitchen equipment. The pan everybody uses may belong to one person; a cleaning appliance may be part of the original inventory. Taking a photograph of the agreed shared items can prevent an unnecessary argument once half the flat has already left.

CategoryDecision to make
Your belongingsHome, next room, storage, donation or disposal
Another resident’s belongingsReturn them or agree collection directly with the owner
Jointly bought itemsAgree who takes them and any payment between owners
Accommodation inventoryLeave it in place and report questions to the property team
Uncertain ownershipResolve it before the collection day

Plan for your actual room type

The operator lists different accommodation options at New Medlock House. Your inventory should describe the room you occupied, rather than use a standard “student room” estimate. A studio’s personal kitchen supplies and a shared flat’s divided cupboards require different final checks.

Pack possessions by destination. Clothing returning home can go into separate containers from cookware staying in Manchester. If you are storing study materials, decide which books or equipment you will need before the next academic year and keep those accessible.

Measure any furniture you purchased yourself and photograph awkward items. Do not dismantle a supplied desk or take a mattress simply because it fits the new room; accommodation-owned items should remain unless the provider expressly agrees otherwise.

Put the checkout date into the booking

Find the end date on your own agreement and read the latest property messages. Unite’s general departure guidance sets a before-10am deadline on the final tenancy day. Check how to complete checkout with the New Medlock House team.

Tell the mover both your preferred collection date and any deadline. Leave time for the room to be checked after loading. If a flatmate is departing earlier, do not depend on their key or their presence to provide access on your moving day.

Keep your own access devices available until the instructed handover. Give the mover a contact who will actually be at the residence, not a housemate already travelling home.

Decide whether to book together

A joint booking can be worth asking about if several residents are going to the same house. Collect a separate inventory from each person and combine them into one enquiry. Label every box with its owner and the room it should reach.

Different delivery addresses need to be included before the quote is agreed. One person’s storage stop or furniture collection changes the job for everyone. Discuss how you will split the confirmed price and who will communicate any later changes.

Frank’s student moving service covers enquiries for room moves and group loads. The Manchester Metropolitan removals page gives a broader view of planning a university move, while the quote should still use your exact New Medlock House details.

Check the collection and delivery access

Ask the property team where a moving collection should take place and whether you need to arrange anything in advance. Include your floor, the route from your room and any instructions for entry or lift use. Do not assume the street address gives permission to load directly outside.

At the destination, confirm somebody will have the keys and can receive the belongings. If your next contract starts later, book suitable storage first and then request student storage transport. Frank’s moves the load; the storage space and its terms are arranged by you.

Check the provider’s opening or access arrangements against the proposed collection. Keep any identification, access code or account paperwork available rather than packing it into the first box unloaded.

Leave with a complete inventory

After loading, check the spaces you used outside the bedroom. Look at your kitchen shelves, the bathroom where relevant, laundry arrangements, parcels and any stored bike. Ask flatmates before removing unidentified items remaining in shared areas.

Record the empty room for your own reference, complete the checkout process and retain your moving documents. At delivery, count the labelled containers and check the loose items against your list.

To request a price, send the full collection and delivery addresses, dates, inventory and access information through the Frank’s quote form. A clear description of the shared-flat details helps keep the booking straightforward.

faqs.answer: Use New Medlock House, 25–45 Chester Street, Manchester, M15 6JX. Add your flat, room and floor, and share the current collection instructions supplied by the building team.

faqs.question: What if a kitchen item belongs to several flatmates?
faqs.answer: Agree who will take it before packing, and record any payment or later return between yourselves. Keep uncertain items separate until ownership is resolved. The mover cannot decide ownership for the group.

faqs.answer: Ask for a combined quote with an inventory for each resident and clear destination-room labels. Confirm that everybody’s departure timing works and that someone can receive the complete load at the house.

title: Moving Out of Vita Circle Square
seoTitle: Moving Out of Vita Circle Square, Manchester | Frank’s
description: Leaving Vita Circle Square? Plan your building collection, split belongings between home and storage, and prepare the details needed for a moving quote.
excerpt: A Circle Square departure guide focused on the correct building, a clear inventory and getting your belongings to the right next destination.
secondaryKeywords: Circle Square Manchester man and van
bodyHtml:
When you move out of Vita Circle Square, give every part of your load a destination before you book transport. Some belongings may be going to a new Manchester room, others home, and a few into storage until you return. A clear split makes the collection easier to describe and the delivery easier to check.

Vita’s official Circle Square page gives the address as 8 Nobel Way, Manchester, M1 7FA. Vita’s property page lists Charles, Medlock and Nobel buildings. Include your exact building name, floor and room in the booking enquiry, and ask the Residence Team which entrance and collection arrangements apply to you.

Confirm your departure with the Residence Team

Read your licence agreement and the messages about leaving. Confirm the date and time by which your room must be empty, how checkout is completed and what to do with keys or access devices. Do not substitute a university’s term dates for the end of your own accommodation booking.

If you hope to remain longer, discuss that with Vita before making a transport plan that depends on it. A request for extra time is not a confirmed extension. Equally, moving your boxes early does not by itself change your agreement or complete the room handover.

Keep the accommodation confirmation and your moving booking together. They answer different questions: one establishes when you must leave the room; the other establishes when and where your possessions will be collected.

Use a destination inventory

Make three headings in a note: “with me”, “next address” and “storage”. Add a fourth for items you will donate or dispose of through an appropriate route. Each possession should appear in one place so you are not paying to move something you intend to give away.

DestinationTypical contents to considerAction
With youTravel documents, keys, everyday essentials and needed study equipmentKeep separate from the collection load
Next accommodationBelongings needed immediately after arrivalLabel with the delivery room
StorageItems you will not need during the gapNumber containers and confirm provider acceptance
Leaving your ownershipAgreed donations or items you will sellComplete the handover before your departure

This is a planning example, not a list of items every storage provider accepts. Check your chosen provider’s conditions, particularly for anything powered, liquid, fragile or unusually valuable.

Separate personal belongings from the room inventory

Vita’s resident FAQs distinguish supplied furniture and main appliances from personal items such as kitchenware and bedding. Use your own room inventory to make that distinction when packing. Do not include supplied furniture in a removals quote.

Work through your room by cupboard and storage area. Personal possessions can disappear into an underbed compartment, a kitchen drawer or a bathroom cabinet over the year. Tick off an area only when your belongings are out and you have checked what should stay.

Keep kitchen items clean and ready to pack before the last day. A half-used bottle or wet mug dropped into a box can create a problem for everything beside it. Set aside a small amount of equipment for your remaining meals and give it a final packing slot.

Get the building details right

A collection request should describe the journey from your room to the vehicle, not just the distance between postcodes. Tell the mover your floor and whether the Residence Team has given instructions about entry, lift use, waiting or carrying belongings through shared areas.

Ask where the collection should be met and which contact will be available. Do not assume a van may stop at the nearest door or that access can be provided after you have returned your key. Resolve those points with the building team before collection.

Our Manchester student moving service can be quoted from the agreed access details and the inventory. Photographs of the packed load and any awkward items are more informative than describing everything as “a few bags”.

Arrange storage and travel separately

If you are leaving Manchester before your next room becomes available, book a suitable storage provider and confirm how the load will be received. Frank’s provides transport into and out of storage; you arrange and pay for the storage service itself.

Save a copy of the inventory and access information outside the boxes. If you will be abroad, think about how you could retrieve an item or change the return date. Ask the provider about authorised contacts and access rather than assuming a friend can collect things for you.

If the whole load is going home, our student moving-home page is the relevant starting point. Confirm who will receive it and keep your personal travel arrangements separate unless a specific arrangement has been agreed.

Close the move with a checked list

Count containers as they leave and check the same list on arrival. Where there are several destinations, mark each item as delivered to the correct place. Keep small travel essentials with you throughout.

Return to the empty room for the final check and complete Vita’s departure process. Check any parcels, bike storage or other personal arrangements before leaving the building. When requesting a moving quote, include the finished destination list so the proposed booking covers the whole job.

description: Prepare your Vita First Street move with a studio packing plan, Jack Rosenthal Street collection checks and transport to your next room, home or storage.
excerpt: A room-by-room departure plan for Vita First Street studios, including ownership checks, collection arrangements and a final inventory.
secondaryKeywords: Vita First Street Manchester man and van
bodyHtml:
A studio move can look small until you start opening cupboards. At Vita First Street, plan the departure around everything you own across the sleeping, study, kitchen and bathroom areas. That gives you a useful inventory before choosing transport.

Vita’s official First Street page gives the residence address as 13 Jack Rosenthal Street, Manchester, M15 4RB. Use that full address with your room and floor when enquiring about removals, then confirm the collection arrangements with the Residence Team.

Pack the studio in zones

Divide the room into areas and work through one at a time. Each completed area should leave you with labelled belongings ready to move and a clear view of the accommodation items that remain. This avoids opening the same cupboard repeatedly because you cannot remember what you checked.

Studio areaWhat to checkKeep available until departure
Study spaceBooks, paperwork, cables and personal equipmentAny device or document you still need
Sleeping areaYour bedding, clothes and underbed possessionsThe bedding needed for your final night
KitchenYour utensils, cookware, food and small belongingsA few items for the remaining meals
BathroomPersonal toiletries, towels and cupboard contentsA separate wash bag
ElsewhereParcels, laundry and any stored bikeAccess items needed to collect them

Do not pack everything from one area into a single oversized box. Separate fragile items, keep containers manageable and list unusual possessions individually. A suitcase of clothing and a personal desk chair need different descriptions in the quote request.

Check what stays in the room

First Street’s accommodation is furnished. Check your inventory before moving furniture or appliances, and ask the Residence Team about anything uncertain. The fact that you have used an item throughout the year does not mean it belongs to you.

The Vita Student FAQs explain the distinction between supplied room equipment and residents’ own kitchenware and bedding. Your moving list should reflect your personal possessions. If you bought extra furniture during your stay, photograph it and note its dimensions.

Give any unwanted belongings an agreed destination before collection. Arrange sales or donations early enough to complete the handover. Do not leave a bag in a shared area on the assumption that another resident will want it.

Confirm the departure time and handover

Find the end date in your own agreement, then confirm the checkout time and procedure. Ask what needs to happen after the last belongings leave, including any room inspection or return of access devices. Keep these tasks separate from the van’s collection time.

If you have booked travel, leave enough time to complete the accommodation handover without rushing. Do not assume a mover can enter the building after you have left, or that reception will hold your packed belongings until collection.

For a move after your course ends, our end-of-term student removals page is a useful starting point. Give us the residence’s confirmed instructions and your complete inventory so the booking can be assessed against the actual job.

Ask specifically about loading

Vita’s First Street property FAQ states that the building has no car parking. That does not by itself explain how a removal collection should be handled. Ask the Residence Team for current loading instructions and pass the answer to the mover.

Describe the route from your room, your floor and any relevant lift arrangements. Keep shared entrances and escape routes clear, and follow the building team’s instructions about where packed belongings may wait. Agree where you will meet the collection team and keep your phone available.

If someone is helping you, give them a specific task, such as checking the inventory or meeting the mover. Several people carrying items without a shared plan can make it harder to know whether a box has gone to the van or is still elsewhere in the building.

Choose a direct move or a storage journey

If you have the keys to your next Manchester room, confirm when delivery is allowed and who will receive it. Frank’s student moving service can be quoted for the full room-to-room job, including the carrying requirements at both addresses.

If the new room is not ready, choose a storage provider and check what it accepts before booking transport. Our student storage moves cover the transport to and from space arranged by the customer. Include both journeys in your plan, even if the return date is still provisional.

For a move home, send the full destination address and details of any stairs, access limitations or recipient arrangements. Keep the belongings you need for your own journey out of the removal load. You can use our moving-home guidance to prepare the enquiry.

Check the room once the load is gone

Use the same zone list for your final sweep. Check cupboards, drawers and underbed storage, then confirm that parcels, laundry and any bike have been collected. Record the room’s condition for yourself and complete the agreed departure process.

At the destination, tick off your containers and loose items. Put bedding and everyday essentials somewhere accessible. When you request a quote from Frank’s, share the inventory, dates and access information together so the proposed move is clear from the start.

faqs.answer: Use Vita Student First Street, 13 Jack Rosenthal Street, Manchester, M15 4RB, plus your floor and room. Confirm the current collection instructions with the Residence Team.

faqs.question: Can a moving van park at Vita First Street?
faqs.answer: The official property FAQ says there is no car parking at the building. Ask the Residence Team separately about permitted loading and collection arrangements. Do not assume nearby stopping space is available or authorised.

faqs.question: Do I need to move the studio’s furniture?
faqs.answer: Only include furniture you own or have explicit permission to remove. Check the accommodation inventory and ask the team about anything uncertain. Supplied furniture should normally remain in the room.

faqs.question: Can I book transport before the new room is ready?
faqs.answer: You can enquire, but delivery needs an agreed destination and access. If there is a gap, arrange a suitable storage provider first and ask Frank’s to quote for the transport legs.

faqs.question: What information is needed for a studio moving quote?
faqs.answer: Provide the packed container count, personal furniture and awkward items, both addresses, dates, floors and building instructions. Photos help describe the load. Say how much carrying assistance you require.

title: How to Pack a Student Room for Summer Storage
seoTitle: How to Pack a Student Room for Summer Storage | Frank’s
description: Pack your student room for summer storage with a practical inventory, sensible box labels, fragile-item checks and a plan for your return to Manchester.
excerpt: A practical packing method for student storage, from deciding what stays in Manchester to finding the right box when you return.
primaryKeyword: how to pack a student room for summer storage
bodyHtml:
Pack for summer storage with your return in mind. In a few months, you should be able to find the bedding, cookware and study equipment you need without opening every box. That starts with a clear inventory and a decision about what should stay in Manchester.

Before buying packaging, confirm the storage arrangement. A collection-based box service may have container and weight requirements; a self-storage provider may have different access and acceptance rules. Check those directly rather than assuming every service works the same way.

Decide what deserves storage space

Make four groups: storage, home, travel essentials and items you are giving away or disposing of appropriately. Put each group in a different part of the room if space allows. Do not mix a donation bag with containers that the mover should collect.

Only store belongings you own. Supplied hall furniture stays with the accommodation. Resolve ownership of shared kitchen items before packing, especially if different flatmates are leaving on different dates.

If you no longer want something usable, check the British Heart Foundation’s current donation guidance or another charity’s requirements before taking it to a collection point. Acceptance depends on the item and condition; do not assume everything can be donated at the last minute.

Create an inventory you can search later

Give each container a short code and keep a matching list on your phone. The outside label only needs your identifier, the code and a useful category. Keep sensitive detail, such as a valuable item’s serial number, in your private inventory.

Example codeLabelPrivate inventory note
S01Kitchen — open firstList of your everyday cooking items
S02BeddingClean, dry bedding for the first night back
S03Study materialsBook titles or course folders where useful
S04ClothesSeason and contents summary
L01Loose itemDescription and photograph of the listed item

These codes are examples; use a system you will understand later. Photograph the packed containers together and save the inventory somewhere available from home. A note stored only on a laptop going into storage will not help you retrieve a box.

Choose packaging for the contents

Use containers in good condition and close them securely. Access Self Storage’s packing guidance recommends smaller boxes for heavy contents, clear labels and an inventory. Avoid turning one large carton into an unmanageable collection of books.

Check the shape after packing. A bulging lid or splitting seam is a reason to repack, not add another strip of tape and hope. Group items so they are protected from each other, and do not use fragile belongings to fill gaps around heavy objects.

Keep bedding and clothes clean and fully dry before sealing them away. Shurgard’s seasonal storage advice also stresses cleaning and drying stored items. Allow time between washing and collection rather than packing damp fabric into a closed container.

Give delicate items their own plan

List screens, instruments, cameras and similar items separately. Explain their dimensions and packaging when requesting transport. Do not assume an ordinary box with “fragile” written on it provides suitable protection.

Photograph equipment before disconnecting it and label the cables you will need to reconnect. Keep small fittings with the item in a secure, identifiable packet. If you own furniture that needs dismantling, discuss that work in advance and keep its parts together.

Ask the storage provider about any item you are uncertain about, including liquids, food, batteries or powered equipment. Use the provider’s actual prohibited-items list and conditions. A container being physically small enough to fit does not establish that its contents are accepted.

Keep a bag that never enters storage

Set aside the documents, medicines, keys, payment cards, chargers and clothing you need for your travel and first days at home. Add anything required to open or access the storage account. Check this bag again before the main load leaves.

Think beyond the next morning. If you have summer study or work, the equipment and papers for it should not be packed behind a roomful of containers. Make a separate decision about valuables rather than sending them to storage by default.

Book the transport from the finished list

Send the mover a container count, loose-item list, collection address, storage address and access details. Our Manchester student storage moving service transports belongings to and from storage you book. Frank’s does not operate the storage facility.

Make sure the storage booking is ready and that the collection time fits both your accommodation checkout and the storage provider’s arrangements. For the wider departure, see our end-of-term removals guidance. A direct move to another room can be planned through the student moving service instead.

Plan the return before you forget the details

Record who holds the storage agreement, how to access the items and what notice is needed for collection or redelivery. Keep your contact details current. If your return date changes, confirm the effect with the storage provider and update any transport booking separately.

When you collect the load, check it against the same inventory. Deliver the “open first” containers to an accessible place, then unpack by category. The few minutes spent labelling before summer should save you from searching through every box when you need a duvet after a long journey.

faqs.question: Should I use boxes or bags for student storage?
faqs.answer: Follow your provider’s packaging rules. Sturdy, securely closed boxes are useful for identifiable, stackable loads, while suitable suitcases may suit clothing. Avoid weak or overfilled containers, and describe any loose items when requesting transport.

faqs.question: How many boxes will a student room need?
faqs.answer: There is no reliable universal number. Sort your belongings first, pack what you intend to store and count the finished containers. Add furniture, bikes and other loose items separately so the provider and mover can assess the actual load.

faqs.question: What should stay out of summer storage?
faqs.answer: Keep travel documents, medicines, keys and anything needed during the summer with you. Check the provider’s prohibited-items list for the rest. Do not assume food, liquids, batteries or other uncertain items are accepted.

faqs.question: Can Frank’s supply the storage unit?
faqs.answer: Frank’s handles transport rather than operating storage. You select and book a suitable provider, then give the mover its address, access arrangements, contact details and the inventory to be transported.

faqs.question: How should I label boxes for my return?
faqs.answer: Use a short code on each container and a matching digital inventory. Add a clear category and mark anything needed immediately as “open first”. Keep sensitive contents details in your private list rather than on the outside.
